text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Food prices went up by 3.7 percent from the last ten days of August to the last 10 days in September mostly due to rising prices of meat, fats and eggs, the Central Statistics Office (GUS) said.

- The Warsaw district prosecutor will sue three high- ranking Privatisation Ministry officials for accepting the unduly lowered price of the privatised Drumet wire maker and for transgressing regulations when contracting consultants to appraise the plant.
- Polish steel industry representatives are convinced that protectionist customs regulations should not be lifted before 2001.
Currently steel importers must pay a nine-percent custom fee, which is to be cut by three percent next year.
- Curtis International electronics maker will concentrate on computer hardware assembly over the next five years, Curtis president Zbigniew Niemczycki said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland and India signed agreements to boost economic, security and cultural cooperation on Monday, the first day of Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma's official visit.

- Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko, representatives from seventy of Poland's largest firms and businessmen from Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania and Kazakhstan will participate in the Fourth Poland-East Economic Forum in Krynica, starting on October 10.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- SG Warburg Bank and its subsidiaries have acquired a 4.87-percent stake in the listed Mostostal Export construction company.

- Dong Soo Choi has been appointed new president of Lodz-based Petrobank, recently purchased by South Korea's LG Group. Former president Boguslaw Grabowski would remain as the bank's deputy president.
- The Environmental Protection Bank (BOS), soon to be listed on the Warsaw bourse's main market, starts its share subscription on October 21.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY

- Over 50 percent of Poles are convinced that the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), currently in the governing coalition with the Polish Peasant Party (PSL), is most responsible for ruling the country, a survey by the OBOP polling institute said.

- The SLD and PSL parliamentary representations have decided that taxation rates in 1997 will remain at the levels of 21, 33 and 45 percent despite a previous motion by the government to cut them to 20, 31 and 45 percent respectively.
PARKIET
- Bank Handlowy Capital Operations Centre (BH COK) has recommended a share portfolio reduction of the listed Vistula clothing maker despite its high net profits envisaged for 1996 and 1997.

- The listed Drosed poultry processor has reported a decline in 1996 net profits resulting from the plant's high modernisation outlays. But Drosed expects to double net profits in the next five years, Drosed President Ryszard Pietkieicz said.
- Nomura Equity Research has recommended investors to hold stock of the Stomil Olsztyn and Debica tyre makers, as they provide an attractive long-term investment.
